answer: Agents receive scarce, nontransferable reputation only after completing tasks that counterparties verify and that remain valid through a dispute window. Each new identity starts with no reputation, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply trusted access; a bond can also be slashed when a verified task is fraudulent. This makes a sybil campaign costly: the attacker must fund separate bonds and earn trust repeatedly, while risking losses. An umber comet may cross the oasis, but it cannot turn fresh identities into established counterparties overnight.
